title: Search a 2D Matrix
statement:
You are given an `m x n` integer matrix `matrix` with the following two properties:
- Each row is sorted in non-decreasing order.
- The first integer of each row is greater than the last integer of the previous row.

Given an integer `target`, return `true` if `target` is in `matrix`, or `false` otherwise.

You must write a solution in `O(log(m * n))` time complexity. Treat the matrix as a single sorted 1D array and binary search over it, mapping the mid index back to a row/column with division and modulo.

editorial.approach: Since consecutive rows form a continuous sorted sequence, treat the matrix as a virtual sorted 1D array of length `m * n`. Binary search over the range `[0, m*n - 1]`; for each mid index, convert it to `row = Math.floor(mid / n)` and `col = mid % n` to look up `matrix[row][col]`, and compare to target as in standard binary search.
